positive.name: the documented statusline payload (code.claude.com/docs/en/statusline.md, read 2026-09-17, trimmed to the keys this script reads plus their neighbours; values are the docs' own: Opus, ctx 8%, 5h 23.5%, 7d 41.2%, spend 62.8%) -- exercises the real atomic write path and prints the one-line status. Written to the throwaway fixtures/window-fit/.control-usage-windows.json through the hook's own --out override (relative path, resolved beside the hook; gitignored in the repo), NEVER to ~/.claude/usage-windows.json: the gate and the guard treat that file as ground truth, and a control that wrote the docs' invented percentages there with a fresh written_at would have the next plan turn fit against fiction (unit-brief-template.md's #0062 clause: use the hook's own test-override for the state it writes). No `touches` entry: the throwaway file is not state anything reads.

negative.name: the same documented payload before the session's first API response: rate_limits absent (the docs state the field appears only after the first response) and context_window percentages null (may be null early in the session). Must print only the model name, never a placeholder, and must leave the output file alone -- a windowless refresh from one session must not blank another session's good reading. Same --out override as the positive control, so neither control ever touches ~/.claude/usage-windows.json.
